Classify a data cube with a TWDTW k-nearest neighbour model

Source: R/predict.R
twdtw_knn_predict.stars.Rd

This is the method for data cubes of twdtw_knn_predict, the function that predict calls to classify time series with a model created by twdtw_knn. It classifies the time series of the pixels of a data cube and returns a map. To classify a data cube x with a model m, call predict(m, newdata = x).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'stars'
twdtw_knn_predict(newdata, object, ..., chunk_size = NULL)

Arguments

newdata

A three-dimensional stars object (x, y, time) with bands as attributes. It can be a stars proxy object, i.e. a data cube that is not in memory, which is read and classified in parts. See details.

object

A model of class twdtw_knn, created by twdtw_knn.

...

Arguments of predict.twdtw_knn, which are passed by predict(): k, the number of nearest temporal patterns used for each pixel (default 1); vote, "majority" (default) or "weighted"; type, "class" (default), "prob", or "neighbors"; and the arguments of the TWDTW distance that replace the arguments of the model: time_weight, cycle_length, time_scale, origin, and max_elapsed.

chunk_size

The number of rows of the data cube that are classified at a time, e.g. predict(m, newdata = x, chunk_size = 100). If NULL (default), a data cube in memory is classified as a whole, and a stars proxy object in blocks of rows with about 50 million values. See details.

Value

A stars object with the spatial dimensions of newdata. Its attributes depend on type:

  • "class": prediction, a factor with the predicted label, and distance, the TWDTW distance to the nearest temporal pattern with this label.

  • "prob": one attribute for each label of the model, with the share of the votes of the label among the k nearest patterns.

  • "neighbors": prediction_1, ..., prediction_k and distance_1, ..., distance_k, the labels and the distances of the k nearest patterns, where 1 is the nearest.

Details

There are two ways to classify a data cube x, i.e. a three-dimensional stars object (x, y, time) with bands as attributes, with a model m. Both return a stars object with the spatial dimensions of the data cube. They differ in the pixels with missing values:

  • predict(m, newdata = x) calls this function and classifies all pixels. An observation with a missing value in any band is not used, and the pixel is classified with its remaining observations. Only a pixel without any complete observation has NA in the map.

  • predict(x, model = m) calls predict.stars, as for other models, and does not classify pixels with missing values. stars replaces the missing values with zeros, passes the time series to predict.twdtw_knn as a data frame, and then sets the result of every pixel that had a missing value in any band or date to NA. The zeros are therefore not part of the result, but a single missing value is enough for a pixel to have no prediction.

The arguments k, vote, and type can be used in both ways, e.g. predict(m, newdata = x, k = 3) and predict(x, model = m, k = 3). They are described in predict.twdtw_knn: k sets how many of the nearest temporal patterns are used for each pixel, vote how their votes are counted, and type what the map shows. A model created without resampling_fun keeps the time series of all samples and has several patterns for each label, so that the votes of the k nearest patterns can differ. With one pattern for each label, the prediction is the label of the nearest pattern for any k.

The time series must have the bands of the model, i.e. the attributes of the data cube must have the names of the attributes of the data cube that was used to create the model.

A data cube that does not fit in memory can be classified as a stars proxy object, which read_stars creates with proxy = TRUE and which reads the images only when their values are needed. predict(m, newdata = x) reads and classifies a proxy object in blocks of rows and returns the complete map, which has only a few values for each pixel. chunk_size sets the number of rows of a block. By default a block has about 50 million values, i.e. pixels times dates times bands, and its classification needs about one gigabyte of memory. A block has at least two rows. The proxy object must be created without the argument RasterIO of read_stars(), with which stars reads the whole images for each block: select the bands after split(), as in the examples. chunk_size can also be used with a data cube that is in memory, to use less memory during the classification.

See also

twdtw_knn, predict.twdtw_knn, predict.stars

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

# Read training samples
samples_path <-
  system.file("mato_grosso_brazil/samples.gpkg", package = "dtwSat")

samples <- st_read(samples_path, quiet = TRUE)

# Get satellite image time series files
tif_path <- system.file("mato_grosso_brazil", package = "dtwSat")
tif_files <- dir(tif_path, pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)

# Get acquisition dates from the file names
tif_names <- basename(tif_files)
acquisition_date <- regmatches(tif_names, regexpr("[0-9]{8}", tif_names))
acquisition_date <- as.Date(acquisition_date, format = "%Y%m%d")

# Create a 3D datacube
dc <- read_stars(tif_files,
                 proxy = FALSE,
                 along = list(time = acquisition_date),
                 RasterIO = list(bands = 1:6))
dc <- st_set_dimensions(dc, 3, c("EVI", "NDVI", "RED", "BLUE", "NIR", "MIR"))
dc <- split(dc, c("band"))

# Create a model with one temporal pattern for each label
m <- twdtw_knn(
 x = dc,
 y = samples,
 resampling_fun = function(data) mgcv::gam(y ~ s(x), data = data),
 cycle_length = 'year',
 time_scale = 'day',
 time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))

print(m)

# Visualize model patterns
plot(m)

# Classify satellite images
system.time(lu <- predict(m, newdata = dc))

# Visualise land use classification
ggplot() +
  geom_stars(data = lu["prediction"]) +
  theme_minimal()

# Create a model with a custom resampling function:
# the mean of the samples on each date
m <- twdtw_knn(x = dc,
 y = samples,
 resampling_fun = function(data) lm(y ~ factor(x), data = data),
 cycle_length = 'year',
 time_scale = 'day',
 time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))

plot(m)

# Create a model that keeps the time series of all samples
# and classify with the three nearest samples
m <- twdtw_knn(x = dc,
 y = samples,
 cycle_length = 'year',
 time_scale = 'day',
 time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))

lu <- predict(m, newdata = dc, k = 3)

# The share of the votes of each label among the three nearest samples
lu_share <- predict(m, newdata = dc, k = 3, type = "prob")

# A data cube that does not fit in memory: a stars proxy object, which reads the
# images when their values are needed. The files have seven bands. The first six
# are selected after split(), and not with the argument RasterIO
dc_proxy <- read_stars(tif_files, proxy = TRUE, along = "time")
dc_proxy <- st_set_dimensions(dc_proxy, "time", values = acquisition_date)
dc_proxy <- st_set_dimensions(dc_proxy, "band",
                              values = c("EVI", "NDVI", "RED", "BLUE", "NIR", "MIR", "B7"))
dc_proxy <- split(dc_proxy, c("band"))[1:6]

# The model reads the rows of the images that have samples
m <- twdtw_knn(x = dc_proxy,
 y = samples,
 resampling_fun = function(data) mgcv::gam(y ~ s(x), data = data),
 cycle_length = 'year',
 time_scale = 'day',
 time_weight = c(steepness = 0.1, midpoint = 50))

# The images are read and classified in blocks of 10 rows
lu <- predict(m, newdata = dc_proxy, chunk_size = 10)

} # }
